elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an affiliate (unqualified)
elements.evidence: "without the prior approval of TrueLink, to a financially responsible affiliate" — the affiliate right remains qualified by a financial-responsibility test

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in interest by way of merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights or obligations ... without the prior written approval of Client"

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and in no event to a competitor of Client"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "shall not give TrueLink any right to terminate, re-price or modify this Agreement"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Vendor's successor assignments remain fully consent-gated: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights or obligations ... without the prior written approval of Client"
No notice mechanic appears; Client may assign "without the prior approval of TrueLink" with no notice obligation

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

offending_extra_words: or of the business to which this Agreement relates
A change of control of Client shall not constitute an assignment or transfer under this Agreement
reasons: Preferred is incomplete on one atomic element: the consent-free affiliate assignment is still limited to a "financially responsible affiliate", so Customer's affiliate right is qualified rather than unconditional as the position requires.
Fallback is not met either (and cannot be mixed in): Vendor has no reciprocal notice-based successor assignment right and no written-notice mechanic exists.

Minimality fails: the edit rewrites the whole clause (37 words to 123), adds a new deemed-assignment rule and extra protections ("re-price or modify", "reorganization", "or of the business to which this Agreement relates") beyond the single needed statement that Vendor has no termination right on Customer's change of control.
Intent is preserved: no undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics, and the surrounding commercial terms are untouched; the loss of Vendor's affiliate carve-out favours our side.
Fix: keep the original sentence structure and delete "financially responsible" from Customer's affiliate carve-out, and reduce the change-of-control sentence to a bare no-termination-right statement.
